subject: Availability verification request and contract exception for PayPulse production spike
messages:
From: Maya Richards <maya.richards@paypulse.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: PayPulse IT Ops <itops@paypulse.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production availability hit — timeline and request for contract exception

Hi Jasmine,

We're seeing a production availability hit against Redwood's hosted inference for PayPulse today. Between 10:48 and ~11:06 UTC our edge telemetry shows a spike of 503s and elevated p90/p99 latency (~2–3x baseline) affecting the payments authorization flow. Impact: several customer transactions retried, ~0.7% of total authorizations failed on first attempt during that window.

We've pulled some artifacts and attached them: k8s-events-logs.tar.gz (node events / kubelet logs), frontend-traces-20281106.jsonl (sample traces with request IDs). Key trace IDs: 1fc2a9, 1fc2b1, 1fc2e8. Environment: prod-us-east-1, model-route: text-gen-v2-fp16, routing policy: latency-priority.

As this incident intersects Redwood's uptime commitments in our contract (Section 4.2), we need:
- Confirmation of the exact downtime/impact window from Redwood's side (UTC)
- Whether this qualifies for an SLA credit and an estimate of any provisional pro-rata adjustment to our monthly invoice
- A plan and timeline for a postmortem / RCA so we can update our stakeholders and our SOC channels

We can share more traces if needed. Please prioritize — this is blocking an internal incident review at PayPulse.

Thanks,
Maya Richards
Director, Site Reliability
PayPulse Inc.

Attachments: k8s-events-logs.tar.gz (250MB), frontend-traces-20281106.jsonl (12MB)

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Richards <maya.richards@paypulse.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Nov 2028 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production availability hit — timeline and request for contract exception

Hi Maya — thanks for the heads up and for sending the artifacts. I'm sorry you hit this in prod.

Quick notes / next steps from Redwood:
1) We'll validate the impact window on our telemetry and correlate with the trace IDs you've provided.
2) Ben and Evelyn are looping in infra and SRE to run an immediate scan of autoscaler and node events.
3) We will provide preliminary confirmation of the impacted window and an initial assessment of SLA credit eligibility by EOD tomorrow (Nov 7).
4) We'll schedule a follow-up meeting (30 min) to walk the timeline and discuss the postmortem once we have the first-pass RCA.

Could you also share: the full list of sample request IDs (if you have more than the three above) and your most recent invoice number (so we can generate a provisional pro-rata credit estimate)?

I'll re-forward the artifacts internally and poke Ben/Evelyn for priority.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

FW: Incoming SLA inquiry from PayPulse (PayPulse Inc. — RDW-4782). Artifacts attached by customer (k8s events + frontend traces).

Summary for triage:
- Customer reports 503 spike and high tail latency between ~10:48–11:06 UTC on Nov 6.
- Route: text-gen-v2-fp16; routing policy is latency-priority, so requests would have tried hot-path serving first.
- Customer impact: ~0.7% failed first-attempt authorizations, several retries.

Can you please:
1) Pull Redwood telemetry (request logs + model host health) for prod-us-east-1 between 10:30–11:20 UTC and confirm any error-rate windows + whether any fallback routing or model variant substitutions occurred.
2) Check autoscaler logs for unusually long scale-up latency or any double-scaling race conditions; check recent infra deploys.
3) Correlate host OOMs / kernel events with the k8s bundle attached.

Please treat as high priority — Maya is asking for an SLA-window confirmation and a provisional credit estimate. I'll coordinate comms.

Thanks,
Jasmine

> On Mon, Nov 6, 2028 at 3:40 PM Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai> wrote:

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Richards <maya.richards@paypulse.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production availability hit — timeline and request for contract exception

Hi Maya — quick update and preliminary confirmation from Redwood SRE.

What we validated:
- Using our request logs and host metrics, we observed a concentrated degradation window from 10:48:12 UTC to 11:06:04 UTC on 2028-11-06 for prod-us-east-1. During that interval average p99 latency rose to ~3x baseline and we recorded an elevated 503/error-rate consistent with your traces.
- Root cause (preliminary): concurrent autoscaler scale-up delays + a fleeting kernel OOM on a small subset of model hosts caused request queuing. There was also a routing fallback that briefly sent a fraction of traffic to a lower-throughput model variant while recovery proceeded.

SLA eligibility and next steps:
- Based on Section 4.2 of the customer contract, the observed availability gap meets our criteria for an SLA credit request. We're treating this as a Severity 2 incident.
- Provisional estimate: a pro-rata invoice adjustment in the range of 2–4% for the billing period; we'll finalize the exact percentage after validating full logs and deduplicating retried requests. (We've attached a draft credit-estimate-ppulse.xlsx with the working numbers.)
- We'll produce a formal postmortem (RCA) and final credit calculation within 7 business days. The RCA will include a timeline, mitigations, and proposed changes to autoscaler backoffs and routing safeguards.

Attachments: rca-timeline-draft.pdf, credit-estimate-ppulse.xlsx

If you can share your invoice number and any additional request IDs, that'll speed final reconciliation. We're happy to schedule the postmortem walkthrough — propose Wed Nov 8 or Thu Nov 9 (30 min).

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

---
Note: this is a preliminary assessment. Final eligibility and credit amounts require full log reconciliation and confirmation of customer-replayed/duplicate requests.
